launcher_contract.inner_run_slot: Requires an exclusive outer start record and real child registration before reservation; cannot independently issue or reuse authority.
launcher_contract.interrupted_child_ownership: Pinned pidfd, original boot/start ticks, live parent PID and exact live argv before requesting SIGTERM; refusal preserves unknown status without signalling ambiguous ownership.
launcher_contract.interruption: A caught launcher interruption requests SIGTERM only for its independently bound, live registered child. This is not an observed child wait status and grants no recovery or traffic-resumption authority.
launcher_contract.known_exit: NORMAL_EXIT records the direct nonnegative child result; OBSERVED_SIGNAL records the direct negative wait result. No status is inferred from a terminal, recovery, replay, pytest or fixture outcome.
launcher_contract.observations: Actual argv/cwd/shell=False, exact canonical authority and input bytes, actual implementation identity, launcher and child PID/start ticks/original boot, actual host monotonic timestamps, observed subprocess result and stream hashes.
launcher_contract.receipt_location: <campaign_root>/launcher-receipts/<run_id>/{started,child,terminal}.json, outside the inner run artifact inventory.
launcher_contract.recovery_snapshot: Original run snapshot immutable. Only independently verified recovery commands/journals may append; pre-lifecycle CONSUMED interruption may append its exact no-lifecycle terminal without fabricated cleanup observations.
launcher_contract.snapshot: Receipt binds the original run file snapshot. Recovery may append evidence but cannot rewrite bound files. The receipt is not inside the snapshot, so no circular hash exists.
launcher_contract.source_test_scope: Only isolated SyntheticContext with owned substitute executables. Constructed/copied snapshot fixtures remain labelled synthetic and are not evidence of actual execution of copied campaign slots.
launcher_contract.supported_invocation: python -m src.orchestration.x6_r1_5_2_launcher --campaign-root PATH --input PATH --authorization PATH --timeout-seconds FINITE_POSITIVE_BOUND
launcher_contract.timeout_policy: An explicit finite positive outer bound is mandatory, enforced through the accepted bounded layer. It is an operational invocation parameter, not a measurement timing change, TTL extension, or new runtime permission.
launcher_contract.unavailable: The accepted run_capture API normalizes timeout to124 without exposing child wait status. Every124 is conservatively unknown. Launcher interruption or incomplete terminal publication is unknown; it never satisfies known original exit requirements.
launcher_contract.verification: Known status is required for public slot verification, including rejected and ADMITTED-partial paths. Inspect-launcher permits read-only inspection of unavailable status without promoting it. Registered child identity must match durable consumption where present; historical clocks are never compared across boots.

not_run_accounting_authority: Accepted prospective single-action accounting authority only; no real authority created or exercised.
partial_terminal_publication: Preserve orphan durable terminal, reject contradictory accounting and recovery before commands; never overwrite or promote incomplete publication.
production_test_separation: Production rejects source-test roots, controlled-clock/stub environments, and synthetic authority. Isolated internal SyntheticContext validates labelled fixture ownership and substitute executables; it supplies no production CLI option.
verification_claim: Every receipt binds its actual source revision; previous full-suite results and replacement permissions do not verify this correction.
